audio_script_it:
Buongiorno, benvenuti al Morning Briefing di Price Alert.

Il Nikkei ha chiuso in rialzo dell 0,59%, Shanghai in rialzo dello 0,44%. Questo suggerisce un'apertura debole per i mercati europei.

Il S&P 500 è in rialzo dell 0,79%, a sette mila quattrocentonovantanove punti. Il VIX è in rialzo del 2,98%, segnale di crescente volatilità. Il Dollar Index (DXY) è in rialzo dello 0,14%, a centouno punto trentatré. L'oro è in calo dell 0,82%, sotto quattro mila dollari l'oncia. Il Brent è in calo dell 1,15%, sotto settantadue dollari al barile. Il rendimento del Treasury USA a dieci anni è in calo dello 0,46%, a quattro virgola trentasette per cento. Il rendimento del BTP a dieci anni è stabile al tre virgola ottantadue per cento. Il TLT a venti anni è in calo dell 1,18%.

In Europa, lo STOXX 600 è pressoché invariato, -0,06%. L'euro/dollaro è in calo dello 0,17%, a uno virgola quattordici. Nessun dato macro rilevante in uscita oggi, ma sono attesi l'EU CPI e il tasso di disoccupazione dell'Eurozona.

Sul fronte geopolitico, la discussione in Parlamento europeo su una legge etnica cinese ha suscitato proteste in Giappone e in diversi paesi europei, aumentando le tensioni commerciali. Inoltre, le analisi sulla possibilità di un'invasione di Taiwan indicano che la Cina dovrebbe superare tre ostacoli militari, mantenendo alta l'incertezza nei mercati energetici.

Nel panorama macro, la pubblicazione dell'EU CPI è imminente e potrebbe influenzare le aspettative inflazionistiche nella zona euro. La disoccupazione dell'Eurozona sarà anch'essa comunicata, fornendo indicazioni sulla salute del mercato del lavoro. Il presidente della Fed, Philip R. Lane, ha tenuto osservazioni introduttive, ma non ha annunciato cambiamenti di politica. L'analisi dei mercati indica che le previsioni hawkish di Warsh non hanno spinto ulteriori rialzi dei tassi.

Passiamo ora al comparto degli asset digitali. Bitcoin si mantiene sopra cinquantamila dollari, chiude a cinquantottomilanottecentocinquantacinque dollari, in calo dello zero virgola sessanta due per cento. Il flusso netto giornaliero degli ETF è negativo, con un deflusso di duecentotrentuno milioni di dollari. Nessun altro driver significativo è stato segnalato. Solana registra una crescita di due virgola ventotto per cento, a settantacinque virgola quindici dollari, mentre Ethereum e BNB rimangono sostanzialmente invariati, con variazioni inferiori al due per cento. Il Fear & Greed Index è a undici, classificato come paura estrema, suggerendo cautela sugli investitori.

Oggi monitoriamo l'andamento dell'EU CPI e i dati sulla disoccupazione nell'Eurozona. Nei prossimi giorni seguirà l'evoluzione di questi indicatori per valutare pressioni inflazionistiche e mercato del lavoro. Per approfondire i temi di oggi, trovate gli articoli completi nella sezione Storie in Primo Piano. Grazie per l'attenzione e a domani.
audio_script_en:
Good morning, welcome to the Price Alert Morning Briefing.

The Nikkei closed up 0.59%, Shanghai up 0.44%. This suggests a weak opening for European markets.

The S&P 500 is up 0.79%, at 7,499 points. The VIX is up 2.98%, a sign of rising volatility. The Dollar Index (DXY) is up 0.14%, at 101.33. Gold is down 0.82%, below $4,000 an ounce. Brent is down 1.15%, below $72 a barrel. The 10-year U.S. Treasury yield is down 0.46%, at 4.37%. The 10-year Italian BTP yield is flat at 3.88%. The 20-year TLT is down 1.18%.

In Europe, the STOXX 600 is essentially flat, -0.06%. EUR/USD is down 0.17%, at 1.14. No major macro data scheduled today, but the EU CPI and Eurozone unemployment rate are expected.

On the geopolitical front, the European Parliament debate on a Chinese ethnic law sparked protests in Japan and several European countries, heightening trade tensions. Additionally, analyses on a possible Taiwan invasion indicate China would need to overcome three military obstacles, keeping energy market uncertainty high.

In the macro landscape, the EU CPI release is imminent and could shape inflation expectations in the euro area. Eurozone unemployment will also be reported, providing insight into labor market health. Fed President Philip R. Lane made introductory remarks but announced no policy changes. Market analysis shows Warsh's hawkish forecasts have not driven further rate hikes.

Let's pivot to the cryptocurrency markets... Bitcoin remains above $50,000, closing at $58,255, down 0.62%. Daily net ETF flow is negative, with an outflow of $231 million. No other significant drivers were noted. Solana posts a gain of 2.28% at $75.15, while Ethereum and BNB stay essentially flat, with moves under 2%. The Fear & Greed Index sits at 11, classified as extreme fear, suggesting investor caution.

Today we monitor the EU CPI and Eurozone unemployment data. In the coming days we will follow these indicators to assess inflation pressures and labor market conditions. For a deeper dive into today’s topics, find the full articles in the Featured Stories section. Thank you for listening and see you tomorrow.

articles.title: The Three Nevers: To Invade Taiwan, China Would Have to Make Military History Thrice
articles.snippet: The amphibious invasion of Normandy on June 6, 1944, remains the largest and most complex amphibious operation in history. On the first day alone, Allied forces landed eight divisions, including five amphibious assault and three airborne, totaling roughly 160,000 personnel. That force more than doubled within days.Normandy was unprecedented in scale but not in kind. A Taiwan invasion would present the reverse problem: Taiwan’s size is not the unprecedented part — the operational challenges are. New research finds that for two decades, capital in Europe has been abundant and cheap, and corporate profits strong, yet investment, productivity, and wages have stalled, and labor's share of total income has shrunk.

articles.snippet: In January 2026 the EU-India Free Trade agreement, often called "the mother of all deals," was officially concluded at the EU-India Summit in New Delhi. This comprehensive agreement, which took 20 years to negotiate, covers goods, services, digital trade, investments, and supply chain diversification. articles.title: Oil Prices Reflect Optimism That Hormuz Has Yet to Justify
articles.snippet: Crude oil prices ended the second quarter of the year with the steepest decline since 2020, with Brent shedding close to 40% on optimism about a peace deal between the United States and Iran. But it may be too early to celebrate, ING commodity strategists said today. Traffic in the Strait of Hormuz is still far from pre-war levels, Warren Patterson and Ewa Manthey wrote, adding that “Total tanker crossings, which include both inbound and outbound movements, are estimated at around 11 on Tuesday, down from a peak of 24 last Wednesday.”…

articles.title: Australia’s Oil and Gas Exploration Set for Renaissance
articles.snippet: Oil and gas companies operating in Australia are lining up plans to boost oil and gas exploration as activity picks up amid the energy crisis in the wake of the Iran war. Australia, which has had to cope with a fuel supply crisis since the Middle East conflict began, is one of the world’s top LNG exporters. Still, it assesses its domestic gas availability every quarter, and the regulators have often raised an alarm over potential gas supply shortages in some parts of the country.
